release.name: CraziiEmu v0.34-alpha
release.notes:
Sonic Superstars, PAC-MAN World Re-PAC, Minecraft now promoted to playable state.

Full Changelog (Click to expand)

 # craziiEmu Changelog * Integrated foundational updates and core architecture from upstream **SharpEmu v0.0.4**, including modernized Vulkan presentation primitives, updated ELF loader structures, and low-level subsystem interfaces. * Engineered a dedicated high-precision display clock enforcing a stable 60 FPS target cadence across both HLE flip calls and internal GPU command stream flips. * Standardized default Vulkan presentation to FIFO VSync synchronization with Mailbox fallback to eliminate screen tearing and lock framerate to the host display refresh. * Modularized the Vulkan graphics engine across independent, specialized subsystems for command streams, descriptor pools, pipelines, swapchain management, and guest draw calls. * Introduced a dedicated asynchronous GPU worker pipeline to eliminate per-draw heap allocations and presentation stalls. * Implemented cross-process configuration synchronization (`CRAZIIEMU_CONFIG`) ensuring settings changes (volume, audio toggle, hotkeys, input maps) apply live within 250ms without restarting the emulator. * Resolved Unity engine rendering freezes in commercial titles (*Among Us*) by implementing flip completion semaphore signaling and 120Hz display refresh reporting. * Aligned `sceVideoOut` event queue IDs with KytyPS5 specifications (`0x0000000000000001`) and enhanced `sceKernelWaitEventQueue` gate waking to prevent flip deadlocks. * Upgraded the Gen5 shader compiler with an advanced resource materialization engine, SSA scalar value graphs, and automatic Vulkan binding layout planning. * Implemented structured control flow graph analysis and data share swizzle translation for complex compute and pixel shaders. * Expanded scalar uniform operations in the shader translator and made strict shader aborts opt-in for broader commercial game shader compatibility. * Expanded the automated test suite to 19 passing test suites covering GPU timelines, memory views, pipelines, semaphores, shaders, audio gain, and input mappings. * Updated verified commercial game compatibility documentation and showcase media covering *Sonic Superstars*, *Dead Cells*, *Among Us*, and *Stray*.

- **Direct3D 12** through vkd3d-proton 3.0.1: `wine: {dxvk: true, vkd3d: true}` in an install script. Feature level 11_1 on the console ([#711](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/711)).
- **In-game menu** on L3+R3 (`[display] menu`), with a **keyboard input** entry. A **two-finger touchpad click** opens the PS5's on-screen keyboard and types the line into the game ([#707](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/707), [#726](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/726)).
- **Single-program titles:** one Windows program as its own app on the home screen, without the launcher ([#719](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/719)).
- **A second DualSense** as a second keyboard player ([#427](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/427)).

## Controls

- Hold **Options + Create** for 3 seconds to close a game ([#720](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/720)).
- The touchpad's left half is **Back** and its right half is **Guide**; mouse **wheel** works ([#721](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/721), [#715](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/715)).
- **L2/R2 vibrate** with the rumble, and the controller stays connected while the PS menu is open ([#712](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/712), [#725](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/725)).

## Memory and fixes

- Games see the console's real memory (12 GiB), instead of almost none, which some games refused to start with ([#688](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/688)).
- Wine's own heap moved out of the game's flexible memory, leaving 5–26 MB more of it for the game ([#470](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/470), thanks to [leolobato](https://github.com/leolobato)).
- Thread and fiber stacks use what Windows uses: 3000 fibers take 49 MB instead of 3.1 GB. 64-bit games can reserve up to 512 GiB of address space ([#727](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/727), with leolobato's patch).
- .NET and SMAPI games with large mod folders no longer run out of file handles ([#697](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/697)).
- Emulators like DuckStation that write-protect 4 KB pages work ([#718](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/718)), plus fixes to audio resampling, OpenGL games and closing ([#699](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/699), [#701](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/701), [#698](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/pull/698)).
- Root certificates updated to Mozilla's 2026-10-20 store.

## Installing

1. Download `prospero-win-<version>.zip` below and unzip it. You get a folder
   called `PPSA99995`.
2. Upload that folder to `/data/homebrew/` on your PS5 and let your loader
   register it.
3. Follow [Getting started](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/blob/main/docs/GETTING_STARTED.md)
   to add your first game.

`SHA256SUMS` lets you check the download: `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`.

Updating from an earlier version: replace the whole `PPSA99995` folder. Your
games, profiles and prefixes live in `/data/prospero-win` and are kept.

# PS5PCEM 0.3.6

This release collects **71 commits after 0.3.5**, including merged contributor
history, plus release preparation. It introduces the experimental native
DirectX 12 renderer, ZAR loading/extraction, launcher FPS limits and motion
sensor input, alongside Vulkan performance, graphics, audio and save fixes.

## Downloads

- **Windows x64:** portable ZIP and per-user installer. The three applications
  and installer carry SHA-256 Authenticode signatures and timestamps using
  the same **Artur Strazewicz / PS5PCEM** certificate as 0.3.5. The certificate
  is self-signed; Windows/SmartScreen can still warn.
- **Linux x64:** `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.pacman` and `.AppImage`, with the native GTK 3
  launcher, `game-run` and `pkgextractor`. See the
  [Linux guide](https://github.com/iStark/PS5PCEM/blob/v0.3.6/docs/linux.md).
- **SHA256SUMS.txt** covers all six packages. Linux packages do not use
  Windows Authenticode signatures.

The CPU baseline remains **x86-64-v3 (AVX2/BMI2/FMA)**. Vulkan remains the
default renderer on both platforms. DirectX 12 is Windows-only and
experimental. Windows packages include the pinned Microsoft DXC compiler,
DXIL validator and license notices; keep these DLLs beside the executables.
Linux requires glibc 2.31+, Linux 5.11+ with FSGSBASE/Syscall User Dispatch,
GTK 3, X11/XWayland, Vulkan 1.2 and PulseAudio or PipeWire's PulseAudio service.
The AppImage uses these system libraries. Games, firmware, keys, saves and
shader caches are not included.

## Native DirectX 12

The Windows library and Settings now offer **Vulkan / DirectX 12**. This is
a native D3D12/DXGI backend, not a Vulkan translation layer. Unsupported work
is reported explicitly; it neither silently switches APIs nor skips draws
and reports them as successfully rendered.

- Shared RDNA2 translation feeds SPIRV-Cross HLSL, Shader Model 5.1 and DXC
  Shader Model 6 wave shaders. Shader/PSO caches retain compiled programs.
- Indexed, instanced, bounded indirect, triangle-fan and rectangle draws;
  NGG passthrough routing, linked varyings, scalar buffers, blend state,
  depth/stencil attachments, HTILE expansion and mixed multiple render targets.
- Tiled surfaces, BC textures, video sampling, packed RGBA4444, RGBA16F and
  R16_UNORM; cube/2D-array textures, mip chains, 3D volume sampling and
  anisotropic filtering. DMA transfers now populate uploaded font atlases.
- Checked fragment loops reject exhausted shader execution instead of
  publishing truncated results. Guest clipping, depth clamps and fractional
  shadow bias preserve the supported raster behavior.
- Bounded resource pools, CPU scratch reuse, exact surface-conversion caches,
  immutable inputs and ordered command groups reduce allocations and waits.
  Experimental retention modes that did not demonstrate a speedup stay off
  by default.

**Terminator 2D reaches first-level gameplay** on D3D12. Raiden IV reaches its
first-stage sequence. Super Woden GP reaches the world map with readable
labels. Asterix and Quake II remain bring-up work: their Vulkan playability
does not imply D3D12 playability. MSAA, general compute-image handling and
other unsupported paths still limit this backend. See the
[implementation and dated tests](https://github.com/iStark/PS5PCEM/blob/v0.3.6/docs/architecture/d3d12.md).

## Vulkan graphics and performance

- **Raiden IV:** retained render passes, descriptor reuse, bounded resource
  preparation, transient uploads, validated vector-only scalar loads and
  indexed snapshot lookup reduce CPU work. The measured PPSA08832 Vulkan
  profile is selected automatically by ordinary CLI and launcher launches.
  Other games retain their own defaults.
- **ASTRO BOT:** RG16F DCC clears, stable prepared storage bindings and streamed
  texture MIN_LOD fix the reproduced colored noise and stale texture levels.
  Long compute loops can complete; exhausted dispatchers are diagnosed.
  An exact NVIDIA RGBA16F RGB-mask path saves/restores alpha bits on the GPU
  and reduces an isolated expensive pass without dropping effects.
- **Severed Steel:** corrected menu presentation, depth-array views, DCC
  velocity clears and exposure-data publication. The maintainer confirms the
  observed black-frame flicker is gone. The local raster workaround remains
  necessary; full ray tracing is not implemented.
- **Super Woden GP:** shared copy orientation and guest vertex/UV transforms
  restore upright interface text and icons. No title-specific flipped image
  replacement is used.
- **OXIDE Room 104:** bounded per-lane FLAT pointer snapshots remove initial
  compute faults. A title-specific virtual `-noraytracing` preference uses the
  game's raster path to reach the introduction and GET UP prompt.
- Scalar condition tracking, base-level storage views, overlap/readback
  diagnostics and opt-in RenderDoc capture improve correctness and debugging.

Selected **historical Windows development measurements**, RTX 3070 Ti,
with their original scope retained:

| Scene and API | Recorded result | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Raiden IV, Vulkan | **86.59 FPS** over 1,800 frames / 20.7867 s | Warm scripted route, October 20; lowest 60-frame interval **50.58 FPS**, so not a stable 60 FPS minimum |
| Severed Steel, Vulkan | **8.70 FPS** over 261 flips / 30.0004 s | Stationary Trash Compactor scene, October 21; 13 FPS target not reached |
| ASTRO BOT, Vulkan | **161.448 → 3.593 ms** for one completed draw | Isolated HDR pass, October 24; not whole-game FPS |
| ASTRO BOT title, Vulkan | **11.55 → 12.20–12.35 FPS** | Same-process title comparison, October 24; optimized gameplay FPS not measured |

These are dated observations, not benchmarks of the packaged release or
minimum performance across entire games. Internal rendering remains controlled

release.notes:
### Fixed

- Ghost of Yōtei no longer freezes after its shaders are compiled (#3). Two causes:
  - Planning the resources of a shader walked the shader's whole value graph again for every word of every buffer descriptor; on this game's largest shaders that took minutes on the GPU command thread, with nothing submitted meanwhile. Each value is now walked once per shader.
  - A few compute shaders became SPIR-V modules of 2.7-3.2 million words that the GPU driver compiled for 15 minutes and more while the game waited (the driver keeps the result, so only the first run on a machine stalled). The largest is now 0.6 million words and builds in about 40 s on an RTX 5090, once; the results are the same, bit for bit (device tests over every buffer format, page-crossing elements and partial EXEC):
    - A buffer load whose format comes from a descriptor the shader reads at run time converted the element in a switch over all 128 formats at every such load (about 130 per shader). The conversion is now one function of the module that every load calls, its field extraction and number conversion in separate switches whose formats with the same layout or kind share one case (`RPS5E_FORMAT_FUNCTION`, `RPS5E_FORMAT_SWITCH_SPLIT`).
    - The dwords of such an element that cross a page of guest memory are loaded with two address translations and one branch, instead of a translation and a branch per dword (`RPS5E_SPAN_TWO_PAGES`).
    - An M0-relative VGPR read (`v_movrels`) is one indexed read of the register window instead of a compare and a select per register, and a relative write (`v_movreld`) applies EXEC once instead of per register (`RPS5E_RELATIVE_PICK`): shaders that keep a stack in VGPRs indexed by M0 have about half the selects.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/keklick1337/rps5e/compare/v0.1.6-alpha...v0.1.7-alpha

release.notes:
**chenxiao07's KytyPS5 [v20261007](https://github.com/chenxiao07/KytyPS5/releases/tag/v20261007) (commit [`9348901`](https://github.com/chenxiao07/KytyPS5/commit/9348901f18a2b3ee5146e2e430f82466f122c34f)) for Demon's Souls (PPSA01341 1.07 / 1.05), packaged for Linux / SteamOS.**

The emulator is chenxiao07's **Windows build, unchanged** (`kyty_emulator.exe` and everything else from `KytyPS5-v20261007.zip`). It runs under Wine or Proton with three scripts added (see [LINUX.md](https://github.com/futbarista/KytyPS5-chenxiao07-linux/blob/main/LINUX.md)):

- `demons-souls.sh`: starts the game under Proton's Wine (or Proton's launcher with `PROTON=1`), with the fixes Wine needs: `WINEDEBUG` not `-all` (otherwise exit 253), `GPU_BUFFER_PAGES` and `BUFFER_RECLAIM` off (otherwise a GPU page fault under RADV when a save loads). It also waits for Steam Input's virtual gamepad and shows the FPS counter (`KYTY_FPS_HUD`).
- `precompile-linux.sh`: the static shader precompile for the Linux graphics driver (about 20 min). The precompiled cache from Windows can't be used under Wine: it belongs to the Windows driver.
- `build-appimage.sh`: optional AppImage of the launcher.

### Quick start (SteamOS)
1. Install **Proton Experimental** in Steam.
2. Unpack: `tar -xzf KytyPS5-v20261007-linux.tar.gz`
3. Put your own dump of the game in `~/Games/Demon's Souls/PPSA01341-app0` (or pass its path).
4. `./precompile-linux.sh` once (and after each Mesa / SteamOS update).
5. `./demons-souls.sh`, or add it to Steam as a non-Steam game **without** a compatibility tool. Use `FULLSCREEN=1 %command%` in the launch options for full screen.

Tested on SteamOS with a Ryzen 5 9600X and a Radeon RX 9070 XT (Mesa RADV 26.1, Proton Experimental 11.0): about 34–36 fps while walking at 2560x1440.

No game files, keys or firmware are included. Use only a game you have dumped yourself.

release.name: KytyPS5 U59 int22
release.notes:
int22 is int21 plus a faster Astro Bot and Astro's Playroom, shader lists in the package, one preset file per game, the latest upstream KytyPS5 changes and work on other games; the older notes are in docs/release-notes-history.md. The first launch rebuilds the shader and program caches once, so the first minutes can stutter. **This build needs a CPU with AVX2, BMI2 and FMA** (Intel Core 4th generation, AMD Ryzen, or newer); on an older CPU it says so and exits.

- **Faster (Astro Bot, Astro's Playroom):** less work on the thread that hands the game's draws to Vulkan, shader code tuned for NVIDIA GPUs, a new profile-guided optimisation profile trained on both games, and host code for x86-64-v3 CPUs. On one PC (Ryzen 9 7950X3D, RTX 3090, 120 Hz; int21 and int22 booted in turn, one boot each, the desktop in use), Astro Bot without game patches: Sky Garden 50.5 -> 55.2 fps (+9%), pirate island 51.9 -> 53.3 fps (+3%), sponge 40.8 -> 53.0 fps (+30%). Astro's Playroom: CPU Plaza 71.8 -> 76.7 fps (+7%), GPU Jungle unchanged (71.9 -> 71.0 fps). Where the GPU is the limit the gain is smaller.
- **Astro Bot, sponge level:** the level's fluid simulation made the game's threads wait for the GPU at every write to memory the GPU had just written; those pages are now copied back ahead of time (`KYTY_READBACK_EAGER_WRITES=1`, on in the Astro Bot preset).
- **Shader lists in the package:** `PipelineLists` holds a shader list for Astro Bot (1,203 shaders, 5,922 pipelines) and Astro's Playroom (324 shaders, 732 pipelines). Press **Precompile** in the game list before the first start and the listed shaders are built then, not while you play. Thanks to the players on Discord who sent their lists. Lists for six other games, recorded with this build, are included as well.
- **Export list:** the new button below Precompile makes a shader list from your own play sessions (`ShaderListExports/<title>-<version>-shaderlist.kyplst`). It holds the list the game came with here plus what your sessions added, also for games that keep their shaders in data files. It holds no shader code and no game data; send that one file if you want your list in the next release.
- **One preset per game:** next to `u59-preset.json` there is now a `u59-preset.<title id>.json` for twelve title ids; the launcher applies it when you start that game. `u59-preset.json` itself is unchanged from int21.
- **Launcher:** other games start with the launcher settings they were tested with (readback, tessellation and the like), unless you saved a config for that game yourself; for that case the game's configuration has a new **Recommended** button, and **Reset** returns to those settings too. The default window size is now 1920x1080 (a settings file from an earlier version keeps its saved size). Also a per-game option "Faster GPU synchronisation (experimental)", off by default (about 1 fps in heavy Astro Bot scenes; turn it off if graphics glitch), and a clear message instead of a crash on CPUs without AVX2.
- **Other games:** additional games now boot. They are experimental.
- **Fixed (GPU device loss during a level load):** a compute dispatch that writes through addresses it computes itself, into memory that had no GPU buffer yet, kept only its first 4,096 stores, and a later dispatch could then hang the GPU. It hit one of the other games in most boots of the fastest builds.
- **Upstream KytyPS5:** 208 upstream changes (through bc934ef03), among them the PSSR pass and BVH8 intersections for Pro mode, skipped draws with an empty scissor, runs of indirect draws as one multi-draw, and many shader and texture fixes.
- **Fixed:** add-on content counts as owned only when it is installed; `u59-preset.json` may contain comments and a trailing comma, and a syntax error names its line (#85); Astro Bot's videos decode on several threads and skip frames that are already late; shader validation uses the layout the device enables and is off by default (#77).
- **Thanks:** the players on Discord who sent shader lists; TheCruZ, Senaxx, chenxiao07, usa-ratt, strxno and Erlou93 for the fork changes ported here; sniperspy69 (#67) and luizhtss (#68) for their pull requests; and the upstream KytyPS5 contributors.
- **Known issues:** rare GPU device losses can still happen; please report them with `_kyty.txt` and `_device_fault.nv-gpudmp`. Precompile builds the listed shaders and the pipelines whose shaders are known before the game runs (about a quarter of the listed pipelines for Astro Bot); the rest are built on first use, as before. The Astro Bot shader list was made for 01.018 and is untested on 01.019; it does not fit 01.007 (title id PPSA21564), which gets the same preset but has no list yet. The Linux build of this version is untested.
- **Upgrading:** extract into a new folder. The per-game preset files must sit next to the launcher together with `u59-preset.json`; an old folder without them runs without the new settings.

## AnyPlay Launcher 0.3.9

Share play invitations you cannot miss, block lists that reach your games, and a safer way for updates to arrive.

### Online

- **Share play invitations now land in Notifications.** When a friend in your party invites you to share play, the invitation stays in the Notification Center with **Accept** and **Dismiss**, and the bell lights up, even when your library is empty. Before, it showed only as a toast and on the party page, so it was easy to miss before it ran out.
- **The Share Play row** on the Friends home page now shows an invitation even when you are not in a party yet.
- **Games that read your block list** now get the players you blocked on AnyPlay, instead of an error.

### Updates

- **A bad update can be stopped.** If a version turns out to be broken, we can now pull it before it reaches you, and a new version can go out to players in stages. Your launcher checks this in the signed update information it already reads; nothing about you is sent.

### Downloads

- **Windows:** `AnyPlay-Launcher-0.3.9-Setup.exe` (installer, no administrator rights needed) or `AnyPlay-Launcher-0.3.9-x64.exe` (one file).
- **Linux:** `AnyPlay-Launcher-0.3.9-x86_64.AppImage`, `AnyPlay-Launcher-0.3.9-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` or `AnyPlay-Launcher-0.3.9-x86_64.flatpak`.
- **macOS** (Apple silicon, macOS 11 or newer): `AnyPlay-Launcher-0.3.9-macos-arm64.zip`. If macOS says the developer cannot be verified, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and choose **Open Anyway**.
- The launcher you have offers this update by itself, on Windows, Linux and the Mac. It is signed like every update since 0.2.0.

News and help: the AnyPlay Discord, linked in the [README](https://github.com/anyplaynet/launcher#readme).

release.name: AnyPS5-ARM 0.2.41
release.notes:
AnyPS5-ARM 0.2.41 brings **PS1 games into the Mac launcher's own window**, through the signed PS1 emulator host that **Settings › Emulators can now download** (anyps5-retro-host 1.1.0 with SwanStation, by B-Howell), with **save states**, an **Internal resolution** choice and the **PS menu** that AnyPS5 Desktop has (B-Howell's Desktop work, ported to the Mac). **A game now starts from its cover** (designed by Lenny4250gh for AnyPS5 Desktop), and **quitting the launcher while a game plays closes the game first** and gives it time to save. **AnyPS5 Desktop 0.1.27** brings save states and Internal resolution to PS1 games on Windows and Linux. The engine has not changed since 0.2.40, and the phone app stays **AnyPS5 Remote 1.23**. Like every release, it is **signed**.

## Mac launcher

- **Settings › Emulators can download the PS1 emulator.** With emulator games turned on, a new row downloads the AnyPS5 emulator host with SwanStation from its signed releases (now anyps5-retro-host 1.1.0). Nothing is downloaded until you select it. The download's signature and every file are checked before it is installed, and again before every game. Select the row later to look for an update.
- **PS1 games can play in the launcher's own window.** Once the PS1 emulator is downloaded, a new switch shows beside it, Run PS1 games in the separate host, and the first download turns it on. Then a PS1 disc from the emulator library plays inside the launcher through the emulator host and SwanStation, and DuckStation is not needed. The picture keeps the game's shape, and the game pauses while the launcher's window is not in front. Two controllers play ports 1 and 2, the keyboard plays port 1, and each controller vibrates for its own port. A PS1 BIOS goes in the folder a new row in Settings › Emulators opens, and a game that cannot start says why. Screenshots, clips and Remote Play's phone pad do not cover these games yet. With the switch off, PS1 discs start in DuckStation as before.
- **The PS menu for these games.** The PS button opens the game's menu: Resume, the discs of a multi-disc game, Save state and Load state, Audio (volume and mute), Internal resolution, Controller, Console and Advanced, then Close game.
- **Save states.** Save state and Load state have eight slots per game, each with the date and time it was saved and a small picture of that moment. Saving over a slot asks first, and a state made by another version of the emulator or from another game is refused with a plain message. Loading a PS1 state also puts its memory card back to that moment. Each game keeps its states in its own folder next to its memory cards. They are for playing alone, and nothing online uses them. They need emulator host 1.1.0.
- **Internal resolution.** The menu's new row after Audio draws a PS1 game sharper: Native, 2x, 3x or 4x. It lists only the values the emulator can show, the choice is kept for later PS1 games, and the game changes in a moment. If the emulator cannot show a value you saved, the game uses the largest one it can and the row says so. Higher values need a faster graphics card.
- **PS2 games stay in PCSX2 for now.** The launcher can also play PS2 discs in its window through an emulator host that ships LRPS2, a PS2 emulator, but no released host has it yet: host 1.1.0 carries only SwanStation. Until one does, Settings › Emulators shows no PS2 rows, the PS2 Internal resolution row stays hidden, and PS2 discs start in PCSX2 as before. The emulator library now also lists CSO and ZSO images in a folder named PS2, and a game's retro.json can name a PS2 CSO, ZSO or ELF file.
- **A game starts from its cover** (designed by Lenny4250gh, who wrote it for AnyPS5 Desktop; this is the Mac port). While a game loads, the launcher shows its artwork with its icon, its name and the moving line. In full screen the cover fades out over the game once its window has settled. In a window it fades out on the home screen, with nothing over the game. It never stays while you play. Turn it off in Settings › Default Display › Start animation, or per game in Game Settings › Display › Start animation. With reduced motion the fade is very short. Esc or ○ still cancels a start before the game's window shows.
- **Quitting closes the game first.** Cmd-Q, the window's close, Quit AnyPS5 and an update's Restart Now now ask a game that is still playing to close, as Close Game does, and give it eight seconds to save. Quitting during an engine build from Git stops the build's tools, and quitting during a call never waits more than three seconds for it. This is the Mac counterpart of Lenny4250gh's fix for Windows.

These changes were built and tested by GitHub CI. They have not been tried on a real Mac yet: please report what you see.

release.name: AnyPS5 Desktop 0.1.28 (Windows + Linux preview)
release.notes:
AnyPS5 Desktop 0.1.28: **a Graphics page for PS1 games** in the launcher's own window, with better defaults from the start (by B-Howell), **Full Screen as the games' default** (by Lenny4250gh), **Polish** (by QguAr71), **downloads that try again by themselves** and stay on screen when they stop (reported by QguAr71), and on Windows **no more launcher freezes while a game's window is busy**. The engine is unchanged: it pairs with **AnyPS5-ARM 0.2.41**, whose Windows and Linux engine (6667cd4b7) the launcher already offers.

**This is still an early preview.** Please report what works and what doesn't in the issues.

## What's new

- **PS1 games in the launcher's window look better from the start, and have a Graphics page.** The game's menu (PS button) has a new Graphics row after Audio. Its page holds Internal resolution, which moves there from the menu's first page and now also offers 6x and 8x for the strongest graphics cards, Smooth textures (Off, Smooth or Extra smooth), Fix wobbly 3D and Widescreen. Each lists only what the emulator offers. A choice is kept for later PS1 games, except Widescreen, which is kept only for the game you turned it on in. A PS1 game now starts with wobbly 3D fixed and the console's dithering removed; the dithering cannot be turned back on. Smooth textures and Widescreen stay off unless you turn them on. Smooth textures also softens sprites and can leave seams in 2D art, and Widescreen can make 2D games and drawn backgrounds look wrong. Settings that do not work in the launcher or only trade accuracy are hidden, and a value an earlier version saved for one is no longer used. That includes the per-game fixes switch on the Advanced page, which is on again for everyone, so the emulator's own fixes for individual games always apply. PS2 games get the same page (Internal resolution up to 8x, Sharper textures, on from the start, and Widescreen) once an emulator host with a PS2 emulator (LRPS2) is released. Host 1.1.0 has none, so PS2 discs still start in PCSX2. Thanks to B-Howell, who built this.
- **Games now start in Full Screen by default.** A game with its own Display choice keeps it. A Default display that was still the old Window at 75% moves to Full Screen, and a Window at another size stays a window. Settings › Default display puts every game back in a window. Thanks to Lenny4250gh, who built this.
- **On Windows, the launcher no longer freezes while a game's window is busy.** When a game opened its window and then went on loading, the launcher could stop answering for as long as the game loaded, or until it was closed if the game hung, because it waited on that window to size it, bring it to the front or take a screenshot. Now it only asks, and leaves a window that does not answer alone: F11 still reaches it, and a screenshot of a covered game that is not answering fails with the usual message. It has not been tried on a Windows machine yet. Reported by Harris851.
- **Downloads try again by themselves, and a stopped engine download stays on screen.** A download of the engine, the PS1 emulator, ffmpeg or a launcher update that loses its connection, stalls for 30 seconds or is refused by GitHub's file host now tries again up to four times, carrying on from where it stopped. If it still fails, Settings › AnyPS5 engine says "Download of … stopped at N%" with the reason, and selecting the row carries on from there. The first-start card says the same, and choosing it carries on too. A file GitHub does not have, or one whose checksum is wrong, is not asked for again. The new texts are in every language. Thanks to QguAr71, who reported it.
- **The launcher is in Polish.** Choose Polski in Settings › Behaviour › Language. A game whose language follows the launcher's then starts in Polish. Thanks to QguAr71, who translated all of it. The new Graphics page is in Polish too.
- **Custom relinker options know the engine's two new options.** `--function-symbol-roots` can be added and is passed as typed. `--to-avx` is chosen by the launcher, as `--to-intel` is, so typing it says it is left to the launcher.
- **The language files no longer list seven texts twice** (reporting a message and its reasons). What the launcher shows does not change, and the translation check now catches a text listed twice.

- **PS2 games do not play in the launcher's window yet.** The signed emulator host (anyps5-retro-host 1.1.0) carries only SwanStation, the PS1 emulator. The Graphics page, save states and the Internal resolution row come to PS2 games once a host with LRPS2, a PS2 emulator, is released. Until then PS2 discs start in PCSX2 as before.
- **Engine.** Unchanged since 0.1.27: AnyPS5-ARM 0.2.41's Windows and Linux engine (6667cd4b7, **Settings → AnyPS5 Engine**).
- **Built by CI.** All five files of this release come from the repository's CI, from the release commit. Before they were signed, each one was checked to hold no launcher test build.

Short on-screen hints and a mini flow strip (`1 · Game → 2 · Mode → 3 · Convert`) explain each page, and the cards are numbered and renamed (**1. Select the PS5 game**, **Converted game folder**, **Launch**). - **The main hub.** Add dump and output folders once, then launch, convert or queue from the list. With an empty queue, **Convert** starts right away (no extra confirmation when it is the only game) and grid cards get a compact queue icon next to it. Removing is blocked with a hint while the queue is running. - **Animated buttons.** When a game's actions change (for example Convert → Launch after a conversion), the buttons cross-fade, and the status text fades in when it changes. - **Game details window.** More relaxed spacing, and the **Delete** buttons are red and kept apart from the main actions. ### Library table view screenshot > --- ## Conversion queue - **A side panel instead of a card.** A **Queue** button in the top bar (with a count badge) opens a right-hand drawer, similar to browser download managers. # AnyPS5 OSX Edition v1.0.0 — Hybrid PS5 + Switch Suite

Native macOS (Metal/MetalFX) port of AnyPS5, packaged as a hybrid console suite with the real Ryujinx Switch engine and an optional OptiScaler enhancement layer for Windows.

## Highlights

- **Native Metal backend** (`MetalDevice.mm`): CAMetalLayer presentation, MSL composite pipeline, **MetalFX SpatialScaler** upscaling (macOS 14+), SPIRV-Cross SPIR-V→MSL compute dispatch — verified on Apple hardware (`METALFX_SPATIAL=available` on the CI runner probe)
- **Full-fidelity execution fallback**: Vulkan on MoltenVK (loader chain `libvulkan.1.dylib` → `libvulkan.dylib` → `libMoltenVK.dylib`)
- **Mach-O relinker output** (`--macos`): PS5 ELF → x86_64 Mach-O with LC_MAIN, LC_DYLD_INFO binds, build version, UUID; Mach-O NID export-trie/symtab patching
- **Darwin compatibility layers**: guest-memory fault tracking (mach_vm_region + shm backing), Itanium C++ ABI views for libc++abi, jthread/stop_token shim, Mach-O export aliasing, dyld-based unwind tables
- **Hybrid launcher** (`anyps5-launcher`): auto-routes PS5 titles (.elf/.self + sce_sys/param.sfo) vs Switch titles (.nsp/.xci/.nca/.nro)
- **Switch engine**: authentic Ryujinx C# source (MIT), pinned submodule, dotnet CI build
- **CI matrix green**: macOS x64 + arm64 (Metal probe), Linux, Windows (MinGW), Switch engine — [workflow run](https://github.com/romangalaxys10-spec/AnyPS5-OSX/actions/runs/36286816977)

## Integrity notice

The `ryujinxemul/Ryujinx-Nintendo-Switch-Emulator` repository was analyzed and found to be **fake** (stub files, no emulator code, placeholder key files). This suite integrates the genuine Ryujinx source via `alula/Ryujinx` instead. Details in the report.

## Quick start (macOS)

```bash
git clone --recursive https://github.com/romangalaxys10-spec/AnyPS5-OSX.git
cd AnyPS5-OSX && ./scripts/build-macos.sh
brew install molten-vk   # Vulkan fallback runtime
./scripts/fetch-moltenvk.sh build   # or bundle libMoltenVK.dylib manually
./build/core/relinker/relinker game.elf game-mac --macos
ANYPS5_GPU_BACKEND=metal ./build/core/relinker/relinker  # backend selection is runtime
```

## Honest capability statement

Guest graphics draw pipelines execute through MoltenVK on macOS in this edition; the native Metal backend owns presentation, MetalFX upscaling, and compute dispatch. The native Metal Draw path is the roadmap headline. "Runs any modern PS5 game" remains aspirational for the whole AnyPS5 family (upstream is pre-first-release); this edition delivers the platform, acceleration, and verification infrastructure that makes that goal reachable on Apple hardware.

The OSX Edition turns AnyPS5 — a PS5 executable porting toolkit that relinks PlayStation 5 executables into native host binaries — into a three-platform product line. release.notes:
# SharpEmu for macOS v0.0.7-pulse

Upstream SharpEmu dropped macOS (sharpemu#1123), and this repository is now the macOS build of the PS5 emulator. Since v0.0.6 the whole emulator has been ported to macOS on Apple silicon. That covers host memory, CPU execution, the kernel and HLE libraries, the shader compiler and the GPU backend. The fork adds 237k lines of source and 168k lines of tests on top of upstream. Upstream SharpEmu 0.0.7-pulse is merged in.

## Platform

- **Native macOS host** (`src/platforms/macos`, ~10k lines): guest memory, windowing, input and display. Per-OS host packages and SDL/Skia adapters.
- **CPU:** the x86-64 guest code runs directly under Rosetta 2, and imports go through a native import path. AGC packet builders and other hot HLE entry points are answered by native stubs inside the guest.
- **Kernel and HLE:** reworked kernel memory, files, sync and event queues, and the host seam and guest memory model.
  - Fibers lock per stripe instead of through one global gate.
  - The thread-local storage lookup `__tls_get_addr` is cached per thread.
  - User-level-thread (ULT) wakeups are targeted to the waiters that changed.
  - Pthread mutexes spin while the owner runs.
  - Short sleeps nap on an escalating schedule.
- **macOS 27:** the OS reserves VA ranges that PS5 titles map. The loader relocates the affected arena bases, including GTA V's RAGE arena and Ghost of Tsushima's batch maps, and maps virtual views into the GPU carveout.
- **Spin-nap patcher:** guest pause/spin loops are patched to sleep. Demon's Souls' idle job workers nap instead of spinning.
- **Display:** the guest render resolution follows the chosen output. There are patches for Unity (boot.config), Unreal, KEX, GTA V, small engines compiled for 3840×2160, and Demon's Souls (its Bluepoint resolution adapter).

## GPU: Metal V2

- **Metal-only renderer** (`SharpEmu.Gpu.Metal`, ~70k lines). There is no Vulkan or MoltenVK layer, and the earlier Metal V1 backend is removed.
- **Command processing** runs on its own thread by default.
  - Program resolution and prefetch run on a separate thread, with pipeline look-ahead across the submissions queued behind it.
  - Encoders are ordered by one fence instead of a barrier after each.
- **Resource materialization** is native and cached. Bindless tables are memoised and kept resident. Repeated lookups skip searches that found nothing last time.
- **Image cache:**
  - Single-copy retile.
  - Write-back of GPU-written images before guest stores.
  - Alias transitions fused, with dead contents discarded.
  - Memoryless stand-ins for colour targets that are only read or stored.
  - Depth/stencil reached on the device instead of through guest memory.
- **Occlusion queries** are counted on the device.
- **Tessellation** uses the hull kernel plus Metal's tessellator, including Ghost of Tsushima's quad-patch instanced grass.
- **Multisampling:** multisampled depth goes through a one-sample proxy plus resolve. A GPU-written HTILE is no longer loaded as a clear (UE5 Nanite).
- **Pipeline cache:**
  - Shaders compile into Metal binary archives, bounded by use and shared across builds.
  - Shader prewarm stores compute pipelines.
  - Guest stores are served while a draw waits for its shader compiles.
- **GPU worker:** no per-draw or per-dispatch allocations, fewer guest re-reads, less lock traffic. Bench tooling is in-tree.

## Shader compiler: gfx10 → MSL

- **Translator** (`SharpEmu.ShaderCompiler.Metal`, ~25k lines) emits Metal Shading Language directly, at gfx10 ISA parity.
- **wave64** runs as two Apple simdgroups. Multi-wave compute groups are bridged across simdgroups and meet at threadgroup barriers. Upper-lane reads and LDS atomics are ordered across the halves.
- **NGG and mesh:** amplified NGG subgroups run as whole mesh workgroups of real wave64 waves.
- **Ray tracing:** BVH nodes are read 16 bytes at a time, with half-precision boxes widened in hardware.
- **Descriptors:** records chosen at run time, branch-chosen V#s, indirect image tables of up to 256 descriptors, and stores through V#s loaded from record tables are all planned and bound.
- **Fixes:** SDWA destination select, `s_cmpk_*`, GDS M0 addressing, FORCE_DEGAMMA samplers, min/max filter samplers, compare samples of mipmapped images, and GLC store write-through.

## Split GPU process

- The GPU backend runs in a separate **native arm64 process**, now the default where it can run.
  - It maps the guest's backing memory and replicates the guest's views.
  - The two processes talk over a shared-memory transport (protocol 2).
- Page-protection tracking is per 4 KiB page. A posted call wakes a single server thread.
- `build-app.sh` bundles the arm64 GPU host in `Contents/MacOS/gpuhost`.

## App

- The launcher is a native arm64 Avalonia app and is the bundle's main executable. Game windows and Dock tiles are named after the game.
- Launcher settings are global, and game settings are per game, with automatic migration. GUI and CLI share one launch configuration.
- All logs, traces and dumps go under one logs folder. Caches are kept outside the signed bundle.
- The performance overlay shows real CPU, GPU busy time and memory for both processes.

## Upstream 0.0.6 → 0.0.7-pulse

- Tessellation, draw reuse and GNM mode.
- XML and pattern game patches, with a patch manager.
- Shader warm-up progress on the splash screen.
- SPIR-V optimisation passes and UE4 ray-tracing shader-call programs.
- Fixes for Saros, Elden Ring, Tomb Raider Legend, NGS2/ATRAC9 and AGC occlusion.
- Simplified Chinese.

## Performance (Apple M4, 1080p, in game)

| Game | FPS |
|---|---|
| Quake, Superliminal, Void Terrarium, Dreaming Sarah | 60 |
| The Oregon Trail | ~58 |
| Poppy Playtime | ~47 |
| GTA V (Performance) | ~46 |
| Silent Hill: The Short Message | ~29 |
| GTA V (Fidelity) | ~7 |
| Demon's Souls | ~3–7 (bound by the game's own CPU work) |

## Known issues

- GTA V Fidelity mode runs at about 7 fps in game. Use Performance mod
